Robert "Bobby" B. Charles

Republican candidate for Governor, Maine · Open seat

Attorney; founder of The Charles Group, a Washington, D.C. consulting and lobbying firm

Bobby Charles grew up in Wayne, Maine. He is an attorney, the founder of a consulting firm and a former U.S. assistant secretary of state for international narcotics and law enforcement under President George W. Bush. He was the Maine Republican Party's 2024 nominee for attorney general, which the Legislature elects. He won an eight-candidate Republican primary for governor in June 2026 after the ranked-choice count.

Where Charles stands

Taxes
Proposes phasing out the state income tax over four years. Has also said his ultimate goal is to eliminate it 'if we could get there,' while cutting income tax rates.
Property taxes
Proposes a homestead exemption and lower property taxes, in part by rolling back unfunded state mandates on towns and cutting school administrative costs.
State budget and fraud
Supports large cuts in state spending, focused on waste and fraud in DHHS and MaineCare. Says services would be made more efficient, not cut.
Crime and drugs
Says 85% of crime in Maine is tied to drug trafficking. Proposes cutting the supply of fentanyl and other drugs coming into the state while expanding access to quality addiction treatment.
Abortion
Opposes public funding for abortion and the 2023 law allowing abortion after viability when medically necessary. Said he would let the Legislature decide what reaches his desk and supports exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother.
Immigration enforcement
Supports repealing the state law that limits cooperation between Maine law enforcement and federal immigration enforcement.
Housing
Proposes tax incentives for prefabricated and low-cost housing and faster building permits. Argues that lower property and income taxes would make housing more affordable.
Energy
Proposes reforming the Public Utilities Commission and using a variety of energy sources, including natural gas, to lower energy costs.
Health care
Calls for higher Medicaid reimbursements for providers and more efforts to recruit new providers and keep current ones in Maine.
Federal tariffs
At a September 2026 town hall, broke with the Trump administration on tariffs and environmental policy affecting Maine.

Background

  • Republican nominee for Maine governor, 2026 (won June 2026 primary)
  • Maine Republican Party's nominee for Maine attorney general, 2024 (chosen by the Legislature; not elected)
  • U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs, 2003–2005
  • Staff director and chief counsel, U.S. House committee, late 1990s
  • Founder, The Charles Group (consulting/lobbying firm), Washington, D.C.
  • Former attorney at New York City law firms; Navy intelligence service
  • Author of nonfiction books
  • Education: Dartmouth College; Oxford University; Columbia Law School
